meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid Federal: Alberta applies common law; Quebec retains residual civil law; federal statutory AML/CFT and corporate transparency law operate uniformly across Canada
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) between Canada and the EU
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP)
Canada-China Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (FIPA)
Bilateral income tax treaties (DTAAs) with more than 90 jurisdictions following the OECD Model

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17, as amended; Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46, ss. 462.3 et seq.; Income Tax Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. 1 (5th Supp.) trust reporting and beneficial ownership rules; Alberta Partnership Act, RSA 2000, c. P-3; Alberta Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c. B-9; and associated Alberta Corporate Registry policies and FINTRAC guidance.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign corporate registry or Companies House equivalent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if source country is a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention); otherwise Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Apostille-certified extract of certificate of incorporation and articles / charter documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Government registrar or competent authority in country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; alternatively consular legalization at the Canadian embassy or consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney designating the Alberta resident registered agent or law firm
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in Canada or in the foreign jurisdiction of the general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization depending on jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized passport or national identity document of every general partner and beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Government passport office or national registry

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incumbency / register of directors and shareholders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary or registered agent of the foreign entity

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified English or French translation of non-Canadian corporate documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Certified professional translator in Canada or authorized translation agency

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence under the PCMLTFA and FINTRAC guidance: all general partners, limited partners holding more than 25%, and directors/members of corporate general partners must be screened against the US OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, Global Affairs Canada sanctions under the Special Economic Measures Act, EU and UK consolidated sanctions, and domestic Canadian criminal watchlists. Politically exposed persons (PEPs) - foreign and domestic - must receive senior management approval and enhanced ongoing monitoring. For MMORPG in-app purchase revenue delivered via Apple App Store and Google Play payouts, continuous name-screening and transaction monitoring are required to satisfy FINTRAC AML/CFT program obligations.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry - Service Alberta (online filing via Alberta Registry agents / authorized service providers; https://www.alberta.ca/corporate-registry)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory requirements mandate a name expressed in Latin-alphabet characters. English and French names are freely accepted; names in Chinese, Cyrillic, Arabic, or other scripts must be transliterated into Latin characters for filing purposes, with the legal element expressed in English or French. The Alberta limited partnership name must include 'Limited Partnership' or 'L.P.' in English, or 'société en commandite' or 'S.E.C.' in French, and must be distinctive through a NUANS federal name search.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Words implying sovereign, ministerial, military, or regulatory connection
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a proposed name, the applicant may file a written administrative review request with Service Alberta, attaching the original NUANS report, a memorandum of distinctiveness, and, where applicable, written consent from an existing legally similar name holder. The Director under the Partnership Act may approve an amended or distinct name. If administrative relief is denied, the applicant may appeal by originating application to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta within 30 days of the written refusal, or re-file a fresh name reservation with a new NUANS search report.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual or serviced office is permissible only where it consists of a physical street address located in Alberta and is staffed during normal business hours to accept service of process, maintain corporate records, and receive government correspondence. A remote-only mailbox, P.O. box, or listed agent address lacking physical presence is not acceptable. For an MMORPG software publisher operating through an Alberta LP, a registered agent with a physical serviced office in Calgary or Edmonton is compliant.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate quantified risk of approximately 3-5% annually for a low-risk software publisher registered as an Alberta Limited Partnership. Service Alberta compliance checks, CRA reviews, and FINTRAC audits may trigger correspondence-based verification; unannounced physical inspection is uncommon but not impossible where a registered office is suspected to be a mere mail drop.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Partnership Act, RSA 2000, c P-3, ss. 51-73 (Limited Partnerships); Business Names Registration Act (Alberta); governing federal statute: Canada Business Corporations Act not applicable to LP structure
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (Corporate Registry System, online portal)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Limited Partnership (Form LP-1) filed with the Alberta Corporate Registry
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for Alberta limited partnerships; capital contributions are contractual and recorded in the capital accounts; no escrow or trust deposit requirement under Alberta law
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the General Partner and initial Limited Partner(s) hereby adopt the Partnership Agreement for the Alberta Limited Partnership (the 'LP') as attached. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the LP shall be established at the address designated in the Application for Registration, and the registered office provider is authorized to accept service of process. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the initial capital contributions be recorded in the capital accounts, and the General Partner is appointed as sole managing partner with authority to execute all filings. AND RESOLVED FURTHER, that officers and agents be appointed to open bank accounts and register digital payment merchant accounts for Apple App Store and Google Play.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (NUANS system via authorized service provider or online portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a preliminary NUANS name search for the proposed LP name and any assumed business names; confirm the name is distinguishable from existing Alberta and federal entities and complies with the Partnership Act and Business Names Registration Act; reserve the name if required by the registry; collect the NUANS report to attach to the registration application.
required_dossiers: Completed NUANS name search request form
Proposed partnership name and brief statement of business activity
General partner's identification documents
Name reservation fee receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or flagged as confusingly similar, file a revised name submission with a new NUANS report and a written submission justifying distinctiveness; or abandon and resubmit with an alternate name within the reservation window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting Partnership Agreement and Registering the Limited Partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute a limited partnership agreement establishing capital contributions, profit/loss allocation, management authority of the general partner, and transfer restrictions; complete and submit Form LP-1 (Application for Registration of a Limited Partnership) including the registered office address in Alberta, name and address of the general partner, and attestation of the limited liability status; pay the statutory filing fee; receive the Certificate of Registration.
required_dossiers: Executed Partnership Agreement
Form LP-1 Application for Registration of a Limited Partnership
NUANS name search report
Alberta registered address and registered office consent
Identification and proof of address for the general partner
Filing fee payment confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or rejected, correct the deficiency (e.g., invalid registered office, incomplete general partner information) and resubmit with a written explanation; if the registry issues a notice of default, file a curative amendment within 30 days of the notice to maintain the registration date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration (TRA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the LP for a CRA Business Number (BN) and obtain a GST/HST account (assuming taxable digital goods/services supplied to Canadian customers); determine whether the partnership is a 'registrant' for GST/HST purposes and register under the ETA; file Alberta corporate tax registration if applicable; register for payroll and WCB if employees are to be engaged.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership
Partnership agreement
General partner's CRA program account information
Bank account details for the LP
RC1 Request for a Business Number and related accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA or TRA queries the registration, correct the BN account details online via My Business Account or submit a written clarification with supporting partnership documents; penalties for late registration are mitigated by voluntary disclosure to the CRA before assessment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account and Digital Payment Rail Onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Chartered bank (chosen financial institution) and Apple Inc./Google LLC developer portals
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a Canadian Business Bank Account in the name of the limited partnership (acting through the general partner), requiring the Certificate of Registration and executed partnership agreement; register for the Apple Developer Program and Google Play Console using the LP's legal name, tax ID (BN), and bank account for payout; complete all banking and KYC verification, including merchant account agreements and applicable withholding tax forms.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership
Partnership agreement and general partner resolution appointing bank signatories
CRA Business Number confirmation
Identification for authorized signatories
Apple Developer Program enrollment information
Google Play Console developer registration details
Company bank account details and void cheque
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or digital platform rejects the application, resubmit with corrected entity documentation or escalate to the compliance officer; for Apple/Google rejection, provide an updated legal entity name match, D-U-N-S number if required, and password reset to the developer account within 15 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licensing and Premises Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: City of Calgary or City of Edmonton business licensing (or applicable Alberta municipality) and Alberta Safety Codes
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Determine if a municipal business licence is required for the software publishing/technology operation at the physical premises (e.g., head office in Calgary); obtain a municipal business licence where local bylaws mandate it; ensure the premises complies with the Alberta Fire Code (occupancy limits, fire extinguishers, and egress) and is certified for lawful office or server-room use where any hardware is present.
required_dossiers: Municipal business licence application form
Lease or proof of premises occupancy
Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership
Safety codes permit or occupancy certificate for the premises
Fire safety inspection certificate if required by local authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal licence application is denied, cure by obtaining the required safety code approval or adjusting the premises use; appeal to the local business licence appeal committee or file a variance application with the municipal development authority.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (AEPA) – no industrial manufacturing permit applicable to ISIC 5820 software publishing
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable – no provincial operating license required for digital software publishing; only municipal business licence and Apple/Google developer agreements govern market access

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – no physical industrial activity; MMORPG software publishing and cloud-hosted digital distribution do not trigger EIA registration under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act, RSA 2000, c E-12
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater or VOC discharge thresholds apply to the software publishing business; if on-premise server or data center equipment is deployed, comply with Alberta's Electrical and Mechanical Safety Codes, electronic waste disposal rules under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act, and any local utility emissions guidelines for backup generators, where applicable

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification required per Alberta Fire Code for any physical office; structural load inspection and building occupancy permit required for any leased premises; workplace safety clearance under Alberta OHS Code (Occupational Health and Safety Act, RSA 2000, c O-2) including workstation ergonomics, electrical safety, and fire drill planning for employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC); federal GST/HST registration is handled through the CRA Business Registration Online (BRO) portal, and Alberta corporate income tax is collected federally under the Alberta–Canada Tax Collection Agreement. Alberta partnership registration is completed at Alberta Corporate Registry.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign or Canadian limited partnership entering Alberta: (1) file the LP declaration / partnership registration with Alberta Corporate Registry (Corporate Online) to obtain an Alberta partnership number; (2) complete CRA Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number) or use Business Registration Online; (3) provide the partnership agreement, Alberta registration certificate, and identification for each general partner; CRA then issues a 9-digit Business Number (BN) and, upon GST/HST registration, appends the RT (GST/HST) program account; (4) any non-resident partner that is itself a corporation or partnership must obtain its own Canadian tax identifier or rely on its foreign TIN, and the LP-file T5013 with CRA; (5) execute a Canadian e-file/e-services authorization with gateway (e.g., Represent a Client) for filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — an Alberta limited partnership is fiscally transparent under the Income Tax Act (Canada): no federal or provincial tax is imposed at the LP level; each partner is taxed on its allocated share of income through T5013; for GST/HST the partnership is a separate registrable person, and general partners are jointly and severally liable for the partnership’s GST/HST obligations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No Check-the-Box or entity classification election exists in Canada; the pass-through status of an LP is mandatory. Relevant statutory choices include partnership income allocation by agreement (subject to reasonableness), election under subsection 216(1) for a non-resident partner to file a net-basis Canadian return, and GST/HST voluntary registration/deregistration elections (a voluntarily registered small supplier may not deregister before one year). Hybrid mismatch rules (ITA ss. 18.4–18.6 and s. 95) override partnership allocations where cross-border hybrid mismatch outcomes arise, but do not require an elective entity classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax); Alberta has no provincial retail tax, so the effective indirect rate is the 5% federal GST only.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 — a person making taxable supplies in Canada, including supplies made by the MMORPG publisher through Apple App Store / Google Play, must register for GST/HST in the calendar quarter in which total taxable worldwide revenues exceed CAD 30,000 or exceed CAD 30,000 in the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters; zero-rated supplies count toward the threshold, exempt supplies do not.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not operate a real-time electronic invoicing clearance model; there is no Peppol BIS mandate, no fiscal API stamping, and no digital stamp duty. The CRA accepts electronic transaction data and requires records to be in an accessible and legible format; GST/HST returns must be filed electronically if the person is a registrant, and platform payout statements from Apple/Google are admissible as source records. Voluntary e-invoicing is permitted under standard GS1/PEPPOL formats if agreed with customers.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Schedule VI, Part V, Excise Tax Act, section 23 zero-rates a service supplied to a non-resident person (other than certain Canadian-property-related services), and section 24 zero-rates intangible personal property (including downloadable software, virtual currency, and in-app digital items) supplied to a non-resident person where the property is not for use in Canada and does not relate to Canadian real property. The MMORPG publisher may claim 0% GST when the game access/virtual item is sold to an end user whose ordinary residence is outside Canada, evidenced by Apple/Google storefront, billing address, IP-geolocation and payment-rail currency. If the purchaser is a GST/HST registrant, the zero-rating may be restricted unless the supply is not for use in Canada and satisfies the statutory conditions.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Form B13/CAED) — required only for physical cargo or server hardware; not applicable to pure digital downloads
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill — required only for physical exports of game media or equipment; not applicable to electronic transmissions
Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent bank/Apple-Google payout report evidencing foreign currency sales proceeds
App Store Connect / Google Play console payout reports showing transaction IDs, storefront country, device geolocation, and currency conversion
End-user licence agreement and digital supply contract containing non-resident status and place-of-use provisions
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA can reassess within the normal review period (generally four years, or longer for misrepresentation/fraud) and claw back wrongfully zero-rated GST/HST, deny input tax credits, charge compound daily interest under ITA 161/Excise Tax Act s. 280, and impose a gross-negligence penalty of 50% on the understated net tax (ETA s. 285.1). For criminal GST fraud, section 327 ETA authorizes fines up to CAD 100,000 and imprisonment up to five years. The exporter bears the burden of proving non-resident receipt; missing or inconsistent export/payout records will trigger retrospective assessment and, in cases of intentional false statements, criminal referral.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada; Canada has no general foreign exchange administration comparable to a capital-control authority. Anti-money-laundering and suspicious-transaction obligations are administered primarily by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC), while the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions supervises federally regulated financial institutions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is generally fully convertible for current-account and capital-account transactions. Canada does not generally impose exchange controls, mandatory foreign-exchange licensing, capital-repatriation restrictions, or profit-remittance withholding solely because funds are remitted cross-border. An Alberta limited partnership may generally receive foreign capital, convert CAD into foreign currency, distribute available cash, and remit partnership distributions, subject to partnership documentation, lender restrictions, tax withholding, sanctions, AML controls, beneficial-ownership verification, and the financial institution's transaction-monitoring requirements. Payments to non-residents may trigger Canadian income-tax withholding, including withholding under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act where applicable, and treaty relief requires valid residency and beneficial-ownership documentation. Partnership tax allocations and distributions should be reconciled separately because a cash distribution may not equal taxable income. Payments involving sanctioned persons, sanctioned jurisdictions, unusual third-party payors, unexplained source of wealth, or inconsistent commercial purposes may be delayed or rejected.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada has no general statutory requirement to surrender export proceeds, convert export receipts into Canadian dollars, deposit receipts with a designated bank, or convert a prescribed percentage of export proceeds. No general statutory conversion deadline applies to receipts from digital-game publishing, in-app purchases, or platform payouts. Apple App Store and Google Play proceeds may remain in foreign currency or be converted at the partnership's commercial discretion, subject to platform settlement terms, Canadian tax reporting, accounting controls, sanctions screening, and bank AML review. Foreign-exchange conversion should be supported by treasury records showing the source currency, rate, value date, counterparty, purpose, and accounting treatment.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for payment collection, foreign-exchange execution, and treasury sub-accounts; low as the sole primary banking solution for an Alberta limited partnership receiving substantial Apple App Store or Google Play payouts. Offshore electronic-money institutions do not automatically provide Canadian deposit-taking, Canadian dollar settlement, or Canadian regulatory coverage. Use is subject to the provider's licensing perimeter, Canadian availability, safeguarding model, sanctions and AML controls, account ownership rules, payment-platform acceptance, correspondent-bank access, and source-of-funds review. An offshore EMI should not be represented as a Canadian bank or deposit insurer. Maintain a Canadian bank account for core operating funds, payroll, taxes, platform settlements where required, and liquidity reserves. Confirm whether the provider can onboard a Canadian LP rather than only a corporation, verify the legal account holder, and obtain written confirmation of permitted inbound platform payouts and outbound business payments.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Canadian banks commonly permit remote onboarding for a Canadian limited partnership when the partnership, general partner, partners, signing authorities, and beneficial owners can be independently verified. Physical attendance is not uniformly mandated by statute, but a bank may require an in-person or video interview, notarized or certified documents, Canadian address evidence, or branch attendance based on risk, foreign ownership, complex control chains, non-resident directors or partners, unusual payment flows, or inability to complete electronic identity verification. The bank account should generally be opened in the partnership's legal name, with authority documented through the limited-partnership agreement, general-partner authorization, and signing mandate. A limited partnership normally acts through its general partner; the bank may require complete KYC on the general partner and all controlling or ownership-relevant persons.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Limited partnership structure is presented without a clearly identified general partner, signing authority, or control framework.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Alberta limited-partnership registration or certificate, filed partnership particulars, executed limited-partnership agreement, general-partner organizational documents, board or partner resolution authorizing the account, signing-authority matrix, ownership chart, and identification for the general partner, limited partners, directors, officers, authorized signers, and controlling persons.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership, foreign partners, or an offshore general partner creates uncertainty regarding ultimate beneficial ownership and control.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified constitutional documents for each upstream entity, current certificates of incumbency or registers, full ownership and control chart to natural persons, passports and residential-address evidence, tax-residency information, politically exposed person and sanctions-screening declarations, and written explanation of the commercial rationale for the ownership structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The stated business is digital-game publishing with high-volume in-app purchases, but the account application lacks a coherent payment-flow description.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business plan, game and publisher descriptions, platform agreements with Apple and Google, app-store account evidence, projected monthly transaction volumes, expected currencies and countries, customer funds-flow diagram, refund and chargeback policy, revenue-recognition policy, merchant-of-record analysis, and explanation that the partnership sells digital content rather than providing financial services, gambling, or cryptoasset services.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large or irregular inbound wires from Apple, Google, aggregators, affiliates, or foreign group entities are inconsistent with the declared business profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed platform contracts, payout statements, invoices or remittance reports, settlement reports tying receipts to game sales, bank statements, intercompany agreements, transfer-pricing support where relevant, expected-payout schedule, and reconciliation showing gross receipts, platform commissions, refunds, taxes, and net cash received.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of capital or source of wealth for foreign partners cannot be established.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital-contribution agreements, partnership resolutions, investor bank statements, audited financial statements, tax returns or equivalent financial evidence, sale-of-asset or financing documents where relevant, beneficial-owner wealth narrative, and independent verification of the originating account and remitting party.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party payments, personal accounts, nominee arrangements, or unexplained transfers between partners and operating accounts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written treasury policy prohibiting personal-account use, approved-payee list, intercompany and partner-loan agreements, payment authorization procedures, explanations for any third-party settlement, documentary proof of agency or collection arrangements, and transaction-level reconciliation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of jurisdictions or counterparties presenting sanctions, corruption, tax-transparency, or enhanced-due-diligence concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Country-risk matrix, sanctions-screening methodology, counterparty KYC files, beneficial-ownership evidence, contractual compliance representations, enhanced due-diligence reports, payment-purpose records, and documented escalation and rejection procedures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear tax-residency, withholding, or cross-border distribution treatment for a flow-through partnership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Partnership tax classification memorandum, Canada Revenue Agency account and filing information where applicable, partner tax-residency certificates, treaty forms, distribution policy, withholding calculation procedures, tax adviser confirmation, and reconciliation of allocations, distributions, and remittances.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected foreign-exchange turnover or derivatives activity is disproportionate to the projected operating profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved treasury policy, rolling cash-flow forecast, currency exposure schedule, hedge-ratio methodology, approved-counterparty list, ISDA or equivalent master documentation, derivative suitability assessment, hedge accounting policy where used, and evidence that derivatives are for bona fide commercial exposure rather than speculative trading.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The bank cannot independently verify the Canadian operating address, personnel, intellectual-property ownership, or business activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Alberta registered-office evidence, lease or service-office agreement, utility or government correspondence, employment or contractor records, intellectual-property registrations or licenses, website and product materials, platform developer accounts, insurance evidence, and management contact details.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital contributions should be transferred from an account held in the legal name of the contributing partner or its disclosed funding entity to the Alberta LP's Canadian bank account, preferably through a regulated bank using SWIFT or an equivalent correspondent-bank rail. The transfer instruction should identify the partnership, contributing partner, contribution date, contribution or partner-loan classification, currency, and contractual reference. Canada generally does not require a universal foreign-exchange purpose code or prior central-bank approval for an ordinary capital contribution. The partnership should nevertheless maintain the executed contribution agreement or amendment, partner resolution, ownership and control records, source-of-funds evidence, remitter-to-partner linkage, bank advice, and accounting entry. For a partner loan, retain the loan agreement, interest terms, maturity, transfer-pricing support where relevant, and withholding analysis. Do not route capital through an undisclosed third party or personal account. Confirm with the receiving bank whether its wire format requires a purpose narrative, intermediary-bank details, or supporting documents. Large or unusual receipts may be held pending AML, sanctions, source-of-funds, and beneficial-ownership review.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Routine operating payments should use Canadian EFT, wire transfer, or approved corporate payment rails with dual authorization, beneficiary validation, invoice matching, and sanctions screening. International wires may use SWIFT MT103 or the applicable ISO 20022 equivalent through a Canadian bank and correspondent network. The payment record should state the true beneficiary, commercial purpose, invoice or contract reference, currency, and underlying transaction. Commercial letters of credit may be used for genuine trade purchases, although they are usually unnecessary for Apple or Google platform settlements and ordinary digital-service expenses. For a Commercial LC, define applicant, issuing bank, beneficiary, advising or confirming bank, documentary conditions, shipment or performance evidence, expiry, discrepancy procedures, sanctions clauses, and reimbursement instructions. Apple App Store and Google Play payouts should generally be received under the platform's approved payout arrangement; vendor, contractor, cloud, advertising, localization, and licensing payments should be made to verified contractual counterparties. Maintain payment files containing invoices, contracts, tax forms, proof of delivery or performance where relevant, approvals, exchange-rate evidence, and reconciliation to the general ledger.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with a Canadian bank or appropriately regulated dealer, used to hedge documented platform receipts, royalty payments, cloud costs, advertising expenses, or other forecast or contracted currency exposures.

Non-deliverable forwards where the currency or jurisdiction is subject to convertibility or settlement constraints and the instrument is legally available to the partnership through an appropriately regulated dealer. NDFs should be supported by a documented underlying exposure and reviewed for Canadian derivatives, reporting, collateral, and suitability requirements.

Currency swaps for recurring or material multi-currency funding exposures, subject to counterparty credit approval, master documentation, collateral terms, valuation controls, and documented commercial purpose.

Foreign-currency options or option collars may be considered for asymmetric exposure protection, subject to treasury-policy approval, premium and liquidity analysis, accounting treatment, and complete disclosure of leverage and downside risk.

Spot foreign-exchange conversions through a regulated Canadian bank or approved dealer for ordinary settlement and liquidity management. Maintain trade confirmations, rates, value dates, counterparty records, and exposure reconciliations.

Hedging should comply with the partnership agreement, lender covenants, dealer onboarding requirements, Canadian derivatives law and reporting rules applicable to the counterparty and transaction, sanctions requirements, and the partnership's board or general-partner treasury policy. Avoid speculative positions, uncovered leverage, and transactions with undisclosed related parties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Limited Partnership annual declaration, Alberta Corporate Registry form)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Service Alberta / Alberta Corporate Registry (Registrar under the Partnership Act, RSA 2000 c P-3)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after each anniversary of the limited partnership's registration date in Alberta
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of CAD 100 per annual return; continued failure may trigger administrative dissolution or strike-off; reinstatement requires payment of arrears and may require court approval.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return (T5013 Summary, T5013 slips, Schedules and Schedule 50 partner disclosure)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - prescribed tax centre
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 5 months after the partnership fiscal year-end (December 31 year-end in Alberta: due May 31 of the following calendar year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Income Tax Act s. 162(7) penalty of CAD 25 per day, minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500; enhanced penalties for large partnerships with gross revenue above CAD 20 million; risk of CRA compliance demand and partner-level gross-up assessments.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory statutory audit for Alberta limited partnerships under the Partnership Act or Income Tax Act; an independent audit becomes compulsory where the limited partnership agreement requires it, a lender or institutional investor imposes it, or the general partner or consolidated group is subject to CBCA/securities audit obligations. CRA may require audited supporting financial statements where books and records are inadequate for T5013 assessment.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for publicly accountable enterprises and consolidated global IFRS reporting groups; ASPE (Canadian GAAP) retains the default framework for private enterprise limited partnerships. CRA accepts financial statements prepared under either framework for T5013 purposes where applied consistently with full disclosure.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta imposes no standalone annual UBO declaration for limited partnerships. Partnership interest ownership is confirmed annually through the general partner-signed annual return and T5013 Schedule 50, which discloses each partner's legal name, address, jurisdiction, and profit-sharing allocation. Transfers of limited partnership interests must be recorded in the partnership register without undue delay; a corporate general partner incorporated under the CBCA or Alberta Business Corporations Act remains subject to federal significant-control individual register obligations.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Partnership Minute Book containing the partnership agreement, consents, and resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 5,000 - 20,000 (CAD 6,500 - 27,000) for a full independent audit; T5013 financial statement compilation typically 1,500 - 5,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23.0% combined (15.0% federal general corporate rate + 8.0% Alberta provincial general corporate rate); fiscally transparent LP is not a taxpayer, with taxation at partner level
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday for game publishing; eligible SR&ED (scientific research and experimental development) 33.33% refundable ITC for CCPCs (or 15% non-refundable for large corporations) may apply to MMORPG software development; Canadian Digital Services Tax Act (CST) 3% levy on qualifying digital services revenue above C$20M (from 2024/2025) may apply if global digital services revenue thresholds are met; Alberta small business rate 2% on first C$500,000 of eligible Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) income (not applicable to LP itself, but relevant to partner-level taxation); provincial innovation employment grant
